text:
mira: quick sync — prototype of the fragmentation-aware scheduler + circuit-breaker finished a short 12h canary. dropping results + open questions here.

devon: nice. give the TL;DR numbers first.

mira: TL;DR: scheduler reduced reactive demote storms by ~45% under bursty embeddings traffic, reduced NVMe small-write rate by ~31%, and improved tenant fairness (99th fairness percentile) by ~18%. small-model tails (<5MB) occasionally saw +10ms p95.

sam: what's the core idea again? scheduler vs simple thresholding?

mira: two parts: 1) fragmentation-aware pacing that spaces demote/evict ops based on chunk compactness and IO headroom, 2) a circuit-breaker that trips when spill small-write-rate + intent-duration > thresholds, forcing tenants into conservative per-page reclaim or rate-limited demote.

jin: how do you compute compactness cheaply? per-slot or per-chunk?

mira: we compute a compactness score per candidate chunk as (resident_pages / chunk_capacity) sampled via a lightweight bloom-ish sketch. sketch update is O(1) and stored in sideband 1B/slot equivalent. fast-path consult uses cached score in request context.

devon: bloom sketch false positives worry me — might overestimate compactness and coalesce wrongly.

mira: agreed. we bias estimator to undercount by design (tunable bias) so we avoid false coalesces. added a confidence metric; if confidence < 0.6, scheduler falls back to conservative pacing.

sam: circuit-breaker specifics? what metrics and windows?

mira: breaker observes: per-node small_write_rate (writes <64KB), mean intent_state_duration, and NVMe queue depth. trip condition: small_write_rate > 1000/min AND intent_duration_mean > 8s for 3m. breaker has three actions: 1) per-tenant soft-fallback to per-page reclaim, 2) global demote-rate cap for low-priority tenants, 3) emit pager if critical tenants affected.

ops-bot: note: added alert template "frag-scheduler-breaker-trip" with fields [node, affected_tenants, small_write_rate, intent_duration].

jin: tenant switching could oscillate. what's the debounce?

mira: hysteresis: require 2 consecutive windows to flip; cooldown 20m. plus leadership lease per-tenant so only one node can flip a tenant at a given time. we also track flip_count to temporarily blacklist rapid re-enables.

devon: what about multi-tenant nodes where two tenants share a chunk (shared caches)? preemption rules?

mira: scheduler marks chunk policy as ISOLATED or SHARED. isolated chunks never coalesce across tenants. for SHARED, demote order respects priority hints: explicit owner > SLA tag > LRU heuristics. we added an escape hatch: if SHARED chunk causes small-write spikes, breaker reclassifies it to ISOLATED for 10m.

sam: sounds good. implementation details: does scheduler sit in runtime or as a sidecar service?

mira: runtime-internal. tight loops need nanosecond decisions. we expose a small async control plane endpoint for Ops to tune thresholds and for higher-level producers to submit hints. control API is a tiny protobuf over internal RPC.

devon: paste the proto sketch?

mira: sure:

```proto
message FragHint {
  uint64 chunk_id = 1;
  enum Mode { ISOLATED = 0; SHARED = 1; PREFER_COALESCE = 2; }
  Mode mode = 2;
  uint32 ttl_ms = 3;
  string source = 4; // e.g. compiler, router
}
```

jin: who can emit hints? compilers, request router, caching layer? do we authenticate sources?

mira: yes those three. internal auth: hints carry a source string and are authenticated by caller identity (mTLS + service account). hints are advisory; scheduler may ignore if confidence low. TTL ensures ephemeral hints don't linger.

ops-bot: infra-bot reports canary deploy: frag-scheduler:v1 on canary-14 — 2026-03-23T20:12:04Z

devon: what's the fallback and rollback plan?

mira: rollback plan: immediate per-tenant kill-switch via config-service (flip to per-page reclaim), global kill-switch to disable scheduler (nodes respect within 30s), and a degradable mode where scheduler keeps running but with very conservative thresholds. we also have a diagnostic mode to force-demote-sampling which helps repro.

sam: latency regressions for tiny models — mitigation?

mira: short-circuit: for tenants with estimated working_set < 6MB, runtime forces per-page consult and disable pacing. we detect footprint using rolling small-window estimator. added unit tests + microbench for detection accuracy.

jin: any new telemetry? ops needs to be able to triage quickly.

mira: yes — added metrics: breaker_state (OK/DEGRADED/TRIPPED), chunk_compactness_histogram, small_write_rate, intent_duration_histogram, tenant_flip_events, heuristic_confidence. also a debug trace that records decisions for 0.1% of requests to limit overhead. playbook updated with queries and example runbook steps.

devon: one more concern: metadata overhead. what's the memory tax?

mira: prototype uses ~1.6% extra host memory for the sketch + confidence bytes at 32KB slot. we think it's acceptable but will run a cost model (dollars saved vs mem overhead).

sam: timeline for RFC and prod rollout?

mira: RFC update by end of week with proto, transition table, and playbook. 48h extended canary next week (50% nodes with IO-pressure adapter on). if stable, staged rollout over 2 weeks with circuit-breaker strictness softened gradually.

devon: sounds like a plan. please include a short formal spec for the breaker trip thresholds and operator steps for emergency disable.

mira: will do. tagging @jin @sam for review. :rocket:
